hero.headline: Hallandale Beach man arrested in Indian River County on charges of traveling to meet minors for sex
hero.teaser: Emaad Mir, 27, of Hallandale Beach was arrested Saturday in Indian River County after deputies say he drove two hours to Vero Beach to meet what he believed was an underage girl.
hero.body:
Emaad Mir, 27, of Hallandale Beach was arrested on Saturday in Indian River County on charges of traveling to meet a minor for unlawful sexual activity, transmitting harmful information to minors and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Indian River County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a home on Thursday, Aug. 6, where a mother reported her daughter was sexually battered by an adult man who went by the name of Adam.

The victim said she was contacted by the suspect on the messaging application TextNow and that the suspect picked her up near her residence during the early morning hours on July 31. The sheriff's office report notes that Adam allegedly had sexual contact with other underage girls who knew each other that occurred between June and July. In one instance, another female victim told deputies she attempted to purchase THC vape pens from the suspect, and when she met him and entered his vehicle, sexual contact occurred.

Deputies created a TextNow account and contacted the suspect while pretending to be the victim who attempted to purchase THC vape pens. Deputies persuaded the suspect to travel two hours to Vero Beach to meet. On Aug. 8, deputies stopped a dark blue Kia sedan near the 1300 block of 29th Avenue in Vero Beach. The victim who attempted to purchase THC vape pens was given a photo lineup and selected Mir as the person she believed was Adam. A court ordered Mir not to have contact with the victim, and he is being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1.75 million bail. Mir was previously arrested on Feb. 11, 2026, in Brevard County on allegations involving sexual activity with an underage female at Anderson Park in Rockledge. He was released from Brevard County Jail on Feb. 13 after posting $150,000 bond and has a scheduled court date in Brevard County on Aug.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
Martin County sheriff's deputies arrested Paige O'Donnell, 62, on Monday after rescuing 24 Border Collies from her home in the 1200 block of SW Alligator Street in Palm City. O'Donnell faces charges of felony animal cruelty and improper confinement, with Sheriff John Budensiek saying she will face at least 40 charges total, one felony and one misdemeanor for each dog rescued.

Deputies and Martin County Animal Services officers executed a search warrant at the property following an ongoing investigation. The conditions inside the home were described as deplorable, with feces covering every square inch of the house. Deputies and animal services officers were required to wear Tyvek protective clothing because of extensive accumulations of feces, urine-soaked materials, boxes and other debris throughout the residence. Authorities said it was extremely hot inside and that O'Donnell may not have had air conditioning.

The search warrant came after WPTV reporting revealed that Martin County Animal Control officers and sheriff's deputies had visited homes in the area at least 11 times since 2020, all related to concerns about dogs and their owners. After the news station began asking the sheriff's office about the house, investigators conducted days of surveillance. O'Donnell agreed last week to surrender one dog, which appeared to be malnourished, giving deputies probable cause to execute the warrant.

Budensiek said the dogs were running loose inside the house and described it as stacked with garbage. The rescued dogs were taken to the Humane Society in Martin County for care. O'Donnell is expected to make her first appearance before a judge on Tuesday. The case comes weeks after a U.S. Postal Service carrier was arrested after more than 100 dogs and cats were found in her Palm City home.

cards.teaser: An 86-year-old woman died Thursday after she pulled into the path of an SUV at a Port St. Lucie intersection and was struck. The crash happened at about 2:30 p.m. at Southwest Savo
cards.body:
A 16-year-old Centennial High School student was hit by a vehicle Monday morning while attempting to cross a Port St. Lucie intersection against the pedestrian signal. The incident occurred shortly after 7 a.m. at the intersection of Crosstown Parkway and Southwest Cameo Boulevard, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Police say the preliminary investigation indicates the teenager attempted to cross Crosstown Parkway against the pedestrian signal, entering the roadway in front of oncoming traffic that had the right of way. The teen told investigators they believed they could make it across the street before an approaching vehicle reached them. However, the driver was unable to avoid striking the student.

The 16-year-old sustained superficial injuries but declined medical transport at the scene. The teen's guardians were notified of the incident. The vehicle involved in the crash sustained minor cosmetic damage. In March 2024, a 15-year-old student was hit by a car making a right turn onto Crosstown Parkway at Southwest Cameo Boulevard and was taken to the hospital with minor injuries.

cards.headline: Four Indian River County elementary schools reach 90% reading proficiency milestone
cards.teaser: Four elementary schools in Indian River County have reached a 90% reading proficiency goal set by the Moonshot Moment, a community-driven literacy program that has drawn national a
cards.body:
Four elementary schools in Indian River County have reached a 90% reading proficiency goal set by the Moonshot Moment, a community-driven literacy program that has drawn national attention. The program was born in 2012 through The Learning Alliance, a nonprofit co-founded by parent Liz Remington, whose son struggled with reading. The nonprofit brings together schools, philanthropists, and business owners to fund added resources, including reading coaches, in elementary classrooms.

When Remington first started the effort in 2017, just 56% of third graders in the district were reading at grade level. Today, Rosewood Magnet School and Osceola Magnet School are among the four schools that have cleared the 90% threshold. At Rosewood, principal Adam Faust said the achievement came down to the final day. The school had six kids to test to make the 90%, needed three to be at proficiency or above, and five of those kids made it.

At Osceola Magnet School, principal Jennifer Norris said students will return to a new campus building and a new reading challenge after the school also cleared the 90% threshold. The school is shooting for 95% this year. Norris said the stakes behind that goal are significant. If students are reading at grade level by third grade, the data show they are going to be proficient readers for the rest of their life.

Other school districts across Florida are now looking at adopting the Moonshot Moment model, a continuation of a mission that started with one parent's child and has since helped thousands of students. Remington said the key is to put the systems in place and build your team and implement collectively and collaboratively. From birth to third grade, you're learning to read, Faust said. From third grade on, you're reading to learn.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce approves 36-unit temporary family housing at GraceWay Village on Hartman Road
cards.teaser: The Fort Pierce City Commission voted unanimously on August 3 to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit allowing GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct 36 dwelling units
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce City Commission voted unanimously on August 3 to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit allowing GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct 36 dwelling units of temporary family housing at 1780 Hartman Road. The project will be built on 7.84 acres near the nonprofit's existing cafe and clothing boutique, with a density of 4.5 units per acre, well below the maximum of 15 units per acre allowed under the city's comprehensive plan for general commercial land use.

The development will proceed in three phases. Phase 1 will occupy 10,200 square feet and contain 10 dwelling units with support facilities. Phase 2 will add six buildings totaling 17,800 square feet, with each building containing three dwelling units. Phase 3 will expand the first facility by 6,300 square feet, adding eight additional dwelling units and support facilities. Each unit will be approximately 990 square feet, and 73.72 percent of the site will remain open space.

Assistant Planning Director Chris Suneson told the commission that the project met all code requirements and had been coordinated with the Technical Review Committee, with all departments supporting the application. St. Lucie County has required the applicant to provide a sidewalk in front of the property from north to south. The Planning Board had previously recommended approval unanimously at a July 13 meeting.

GraceWay Village CEO Chrystal Netherton told the Planning Board in July that the facility focuses on temporary stays to help families become self-sufficient. Project Engineer Mark Landsman said many residents might only need a three-month stay. Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky made the motion for approval on August 3, which was seconded by Commissioner Michael Broderick and passed unanimously.

cards.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
cards.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway i
cards.body:
Josiah Baur, 23, rescued a woman whose car became trapped on train tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening, lifting the crossing gate seconds before a freight train passed through. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm suddenly came down on her car, leaving her stuck between the gates. Dash-cam video captured the tense moments as a train's horn sounded while it moved closer to Spoelstra's red car.

Baur was leaving work and heading home to Port Saint Lucie when he stopped at the crossing on the other side of the tracks. He saw the car stuck and Spoelstra still inside, threw his car in park and ran across the tracks. He looked to see which side the train was on, saw it was on her side, and lifted the gate with both arms to release her car just in time for her to back up before the train came through.

Spoelstra said she put her car in reverse but the gate got stuck on top of her car on the antenna, preventing her from backing up. A witness, Lizzy Dominguez, was behind Baur's car and took a photo of him after the rescue, posting it on social media to find and thank him. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday and hugged. Spoelstra says her baby grandson shares the same name as the man who saved her: Josiah.

cards.headline: Indian River County school enrollment exceeds state projections with expanded programs
cards.teaser: Indian River County schools are starting the year with enrollment expected to exceed the state's projections, thanks to expanded programs and a focus on listening to families.
cards.body:
Indian River County school leaders say they are starting the year with enrollment expected to exceed the state's projections, thanks to expanded programs and a focus on listening to families. About 14,000 students are expected to begin the school year across the district. Liberty Magnet School is welcoming about 650 students this year, roughly the same as last year. Principal Chris Taylor said he is happy to see the halls full again after a quiet summer.

David Moore said the district has expanded its magnet and K-8 options to better meet families' needs. The district has also implemented other strategies to attract and retain families, including creating programming for homeschool students, removing attendance boundaries, and utilizing open choice. Moore said the district took time to sit back, relax, and understand what the community wants when it comes to educating children.

Moore said the district still sees a slight decline in enrollment year after year, but it is not significant enough to impact the budget. The Hamilton family said the support their children receive at Liberty Magnet keeps them coming back. All three of their children have gone to the school, and the school has been really invested in their success, parent Matt Hamilton said.

hero.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
hero.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.headline: Florida awards $1 million to fire departments for cancer prevention equipment
hero.teaser: Florida Chief Financial Officer Jimmy Ingoglia announced Monday the allocation of $1 million to fire departments across the state through programs designed to protect firefighters
hero.body:
Florida Chief Financial Officer Jimmy Ingoglia announced Monday the allocation of $1 million to fire departments across the state through programs designed to protect firefighters from cancer-causing chemicals. Ingoglia made the announcement at West Palm Beach Fire Station 1, joined by state Rep. Anne Gerwig, state Rep. Peggy Gossett-Seidman, and West Palm Beach Mayor Keith James. The funds come from the Firefighter Cancer Decontamination Grant Program, the Firefighter Assistance Grant Program, and projects appropriated in the state's fiscal 2025-2026 budget.

The program provides financial assistance to fire departments, including volunteer departments, to procure equipment, supplies, and educational training designed to mitigate exposure to hazardous, cancer-causing chemicals. Ingoglia explained that modern fires pose greater health risks than decades ago because burning structures now contain materials beyond wood and concrete that release substances absorbed through the skin, eyes, and lungs of firefighters. West Palm Beach received $19,635, Greenacres received $6,806, and Highland Beach received $5,962 from Monday's allocation. West Palm Beach Fire Chief Diana Matty said the grants fund second sets of gloves, particulate blocking hoods, on-scene cleansing wipes, and specialized washers.

The state still has $1 million available through the Firefighter Cancer Decontamination Grant Program and another $1 million available for the Firefighter Assistance Grant Program in this year's state budget. Ingoglia urged fire chiefs across Florida to apply for the remaining funds.

Ingoglia also addressed concerns about an upcoming property tax amendment vote and funding worries expressed by cities and first responders. He said county budgets have increased between 60 to 160 percent over the past six years and counties have benefited from historic property tax revenue. Ingoglia stated he believes there is room to offer property tax relief while still funding necessary items for first responders, despite anxiety from sheriffs, police chiefs, and fire chiefs about potential budget cuts and layoffs. He said the vast majority of their budgets are controlled by county commissioners or mayors and there is more than enough money available.

cards.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
cards.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway i
cards.body:
Josiah Baur, 23, rescued a woman whose car became trapped on train tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening, lifting the crossing gate seconds before a freight train passed through. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm suddenly came down on her car, leaving her stuck between the gates. Dash-cam video captured the tense moments as a train's horn sounded while it moved closer to Spoelstra's red car.

Baur was leaving work and heading home to Port Saint Lucie when he stopped at the crossing on the other side of the tracks. He saw the car stuck and Spoelstra still inside, threw his car in park and ran across the tracks. He looked to see which side the train was on, saw it was on her side, and lifted the gate with both arms to release her car just in time for her to back up before the train came through.

Spoelstra said she put her car in reverse but the gate got stuck on top of her car on the antenna, preventing her from backing up. A witness, Lizzy Dominguez, was behind Baur's car and took a photo of him after the rescue, posting it on social media to find and thank him. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday and hugged. Spoelstra says her baby grandson shares the same name as the man who saved her: Josiah.

cards.headline: More Than 70 Animals Found in Stuart Home During Large-Scale Hoarding Response
cards.teaser: 77-year-old Gail Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges following the search of a Stuart home where Martin County authorities found more than 70 an
cards.body:
Martin County sheriff's deputies arrested Paige O'Donnell, 62, on Monday after rescuing 24 Border Collies from her home in the 1200 block of SW Alligator Street in Palm City. O'Donnell faces charges of felony animal cruelty and improper confinement, with Sheriff John Budensiek saying she will face at least 40 charges total, one felony and one misdemeanor for each dog rescued.

Deputies and Martin County Animal Services officers executed a search warrant at the property following an ongoing investigation. The conditions inside the home were described as deplorable, with feces covering every square inch of the house. Deputies and animal services officers were required to wear Tyvek protective clothing because of extensive accumulations of feces, urine-soaked materials, boxes and other debris throughout the residence. Authorities said it was extremely hot inside and that O'Donnell may not have had air conditioning.

The search warrant came after WPTV reporting revealed that Martin County Animal Control officers and sheriff's deputies had visited homes in the area at least 11 times since 2020, all related to concerns about dogs and their owners. After the news station began asking the sheriff's office about the house, investigators conducted days of surveillance. O'Donnell agreed last week to surrender one dog, which appeared to be malnourished, giving deputies probable cause to execute the warrant.

Budensiek said the dogs were running loose inside the house and described it as stacked with garbage. The rescued dogs were taken to the Humane Society in Martin County for care. O'Donnell is expected to make her first appearance before a judge on Tuesday. The case comes weeks after a U.S. Postal Service carrier was arrested after more than 100 dogs and cats were found in her Palm City home.

hero.headline: Four Indian River County elementary schools reach 90% reading proficiency milestone
hero.teaser: Four elementary schools in Indian River County have reached a 90% reading proficiency goal set by the Moonshot Moment, a community-driven literacy program that has drawn national a
hero.body:
Four elementary schools in Indian River County have reached a 90% reading proficiency goal set by the Moonshot Moment, a community-driven literacy program that has drawn national attention. The program was born in 2012 through The Learning Alliance, a nonprofit co-founded by parent Liz Remington, whose son struggled with reading. The nonprofit brings together schools, philanthropists, and business owners to fund added resources, including reading coaches, in elementary classrooms.

When Remington first started the effort in 2017, just 56% of third graders in the district were reading at grade level. Today, Rosewood Magnet School and Osceola Magnet School are among the four schools that have cleared the 90% threshold. At Rosewood, principal Adam Faust said the achievement came down to the final day. The school had six kids to test to make the 90%, needed three to be at proficiency or above, and five of those kids made it.

At Osceola Magnet School, principal Jennifer Norris said students will return to a new campus building and a new reading challenge after the school also cleared the 90% threshold. The school is shooting for 95% this year. Norris said the stakes behind that goal are significant. If students are reading at grade level by third grade, the data show they are going to be proficient readers for the rest of their life.

Other school districts across Florida are now looking at adopting the Moonshot Moment model, a continuation of a mission that started with one parent's child and has since helped thousands of students. Remington said the key is to put the systems in place and build your team and implement collectively and collaboratively. From birth to third grade, you're learning to read, Faust said. From third grade on, you're reading to learn.

cards.headline: Indian River County school enrollment exceeds state projections with expanded programs
cards.teaser: Indian River County schools are starting the year with enrollment expected to exceed the state's projections, thanks to expanded programs and a focus on listening to families.
cards.body:
Indian River County school leaders say they are starting the year with enrollment expected to exceed the state's projections, thanks to expanded programs and a focus on listening to families. About 14,000 students are expected to begin the school year across the district. Liberty Magnet School is welcoming about 650 students this year, roughly the same as last year. Principal Chris Taylor said he is happy to see the halls full again after a quiet summer.

David Moore said the district has expanded its magnet and K-8 options to better meet families' needs. The district has also implemented other strategies to attract and retain families, including creating programming for homeschool students, removing attendance boundaries, and utilizing open choice. Moore said the district took time to sit back, relax, and understand what the community wants when it comes to educating children.

Moore said the district still sees a slight decline in enrollment year after year, but it is not significant enough to impact the budget. The Hamilton family said the support their children receive at Liberty Magnet keeps them coming back. All three of their children have gone to the school, and the school has been really invested in their success, parent Matt Hamilton said.

cards.headline: Hallandale Beach man arrested in Indian River County on charges of traveling to meet minors for sex
cards.teaser: Emaad Mir, 27, of Hallandale Beach was arrested Saturday in Indian River County after deputies say he drove two hours to Vero Beach to meet what he believed was an underage girl.
cards.body:
Emaad Mir, 27, from Hallandale Beach, was arrested on Saturday, Aug. 8 on charges of traveling to meet a minor for unlawful sexual activity, transmitting harmful information to minors and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Two Indian River County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a home on Thursday, Aug. 6, where they were told by a mother that her daughter was sexually battered by an adult man who went by the name of Adam. The victim said she believed the suspect was 21 years old and was contacted by the person on the messaging application TextNow.

The victim said she and the suspect arranged for Adam to pick her up near her residence during the early morning hours on July 31. Inside the suspect's vehicle, sexual contact occurred. The sheriff's office report notes that Adam allegedly had sexual contact with other underage girls who knew each other that occurred between June and July. Deputies created a TextNow account and used their phone to contact the suspect on the app. Pretending to be a victim, deputies persuaded the suspect to travel two hours to Vero Beach to meet. Deputies stopped a dark blue Kia sedan near the 1300 block of 29th Avenue and took the suspect into custody. Deputies determined the driver of the Kia was Mir.

During a court hearing on Sunday, Aug. 9, a court ordered Mir not to have contact with the vape pen victim, and he is being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1.75 million bail. This was not the first time Mir was accused of sexual activity with an underage girl. He was arrested on Feb. 11, 2026 by Rockledge Police on allegations that an officer observed a suspicious vehicle at Anderson Park at 12:48 a.m. Mir faces charges of lewd or lascivious battery of a victim between the ages of 12 and 16 years old and traveling to meet a minor after luring by computer in Brevard County. Mir has a scheduled court date in Brevard County on Aug. 11.

cards.headline: Indian River County converts Freshman Learning Center into Vero Beach Middle School
cards.teaser: The Freshman Learning Center has been converted into Vero Beach Middle School as Indian River County school leaders reorganize schools ahead of the new year.
cards.body:
A different approach to public education is taking shape in Indian River County this school year as district leaders expand school choice and reorganize several campuses. The Freshman Learning Center has been converted into Vero Beach Middle School. Moore says the freshman center was expensive to operate and did not provide students with high-quality educational programs. He says moving ninth-graders back to traditional high schools will also give them earlier access to more academic opportunities.

From a student's perspective, moving ninth-graders back allows them access to programming that was only being offered at the high school. Students should not have to wait until they are in 10th grade to take some of those courses, Moore said. District leaders say the two high schools, Sebastian River High School and Vero Beach High School, have enough capacity to accommodate incoming freshmen. That means all incoming ninth-graders this school year will attend either Sebastian River High School or Vero Beach High School.

Families in the district have more flexibility in where their children attend school. Parents can choose to enroll their children at schools across the district, rather than being limited to the school assigned to their neighborhood. The district has also converted several campuses into K-8 schools and operates five charter schools. The changes are part of the district's broader effort to give families more educational options while restructuring how its schools serve students.

cards.headline: Vero Beach High School marching band prepares for school year with nearly 90 years of tradition
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach High School Fighting Indians Band is preparing for the new school year as students practice at band camp just days before classes resume. The program was founded in
cards.body:
The Vero Beach High School Fighting Indians Band held band camp at the school just a few days before school started. The band was founded in 1934 as part of the Federal Music Project during the Great Depression. Band director Sean Srigley is an alumnus of Vero Beach High School and was in the band himself. Srigley said the band has awesome academics and awesome athletics, and the band is right there with them. The band has marched in pretty much every big parade you could have in America.

The band performed in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in 1988, marching through the streets of New York City and playing Alexander's Ragtime Band for millions of television viewers. That single performance became one of the defining moments in the program's history and remains a source of pride for every new generation of members. The band has also performed in the Tournament of Roses Parade, the Fiesta Bowl Parade, the Orange Bowl and even Carnegie Hall. The program has earned decades of Superior ratings and national recognition while representing the Treasure Coast with pride.

Annabel Robbins plays flute piccolo and is a drum major. Brady, an incoming senior, is the woodwind captain and section leader. Brady said being in charge of a lot of kids is kind of scary, and you have to make sure they are all doing good. Joining the marching band for practice means discipline and the ability to stand for a long time in the Florida heat, something these kids do with incredible dedication.
